name: Diagram build
one_line: A node-and-link diagram assembled piece by piece, earlier parts receding as new ones arrive
summary: A structure or sequence is taught one piece at a time: each node and connector arrives in turn while the parts already explained dim into the background. The viewer meets the whole only after learning its parts. Too many pieces per beat, or earlier parts vanishing rather than receding, loses the thread.

routes.one_line: Place a few nodes by hand and reveal nodes and connectors in turn on one Anime.js timeline

steps.does: Reveal each node, draw each connector before it, and dim earlier nodes on one seekable timeline

limits: Suits a handful of nodes; positions are yours to set, so nothing reflows when a label changes
Receding by tweening colours proved fragile in a build; fading a separate overlay per node held
Evidence covers one path draw and one stagger, not a multi-node build

routes.one_line: Lay the diagram out with Graphviz, then reveal its nodes and edges in turn

steps.does: Lay out the nodes and edges automatically and emit SVG
Reveal and dim the SVG's nodes and edges on a seekable timeline

limits: Graphviz evidence is one four-node graph; larger graphs and animating its generated ids are untested
Anime.js evidence covers one path draw and one stagger, not a full node-and-edge build
Automatic layout gives no control over where each piece lands relative to narration

routes.one_line: Compute node positions with D3 geometry, draw as SVG and animate the arrivals

steps.does: Compute node and link geometry from a hierarchy or graph
Reveal and dim the drawn nodes and links on a seekable timeline

limits: D3 evidence is a bar-and-line chart; hierarchy and force layouts are untested
Force layouts are iterative and must be run to a fixed result before frames are seeked

routes.one_line: Author the build as a generator scene with its own 2D scene graph

steps.does: Sequence each node and connector arrival in a generator-based scene

limits: Evidence is editor PNG-sequence export; a diagram scene and headless runs are untested
It is a separate project environment, not a layer inside an existing page

source: references/pacing-editor §4, references/motion-director §4.2, references/art-director §5.3; tool records as of 2026-11-20
